newsitem.title: USA: Glickman says USDA to buy $30 mln additional beef.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says USDA to buy $30 mln additional beef.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Secretary Dan Glickman said the government will buy an additional $30 million of beef for domestic distribution to help reduce current burdensome supply of processing beef.

"The Clinton Administration is taking this additional step to help bolster low slaughter cow prices and to help minimize the impact of anticipated seasonal increases in cow slaughter on beef prices," Glickman said.

The USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service is to begin buying frozen ground beef, canned beef with natural juices, and processing beef produced from the round for distribution to schools and recipients in other food assistance programs.

Since May 1, when Glickman announced accelerated federal beef purchasing as a way to aid the cattle industry, the government has bought about 75 million pounds of beef products at a cost of about $70 million.

The USDA also offered nearly $40 million to help drought-stricken producers in the Southwest feed livestock, named a special advisory committee to review corporate concentration in agriculture, and expanded reporting by AMS on beef carcass-based pricing, forward sales, and boxed beef.
